Definition: Achashverosh (i.e. Ahasuerus or Artaxerxes, but in this case Xerxes), the title (rather than name) of a Persian king
BiblicalUsage: Ahasuerus — Achashverosh in the Hebrew — is the Persian king of Esther's story, reigning from India even unto Ethiopia, and the same name appears in Ezra and Daniel.
TheologicalSignificance: The name itself teaches nothing, but the throne it sat on is the stage for one of Scripture's clearest pictures of hidden providence: a pagan king, a Jewish queen, and a God who is never named yet moves every piece.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
